usageNotes: Use this to list all cluster-level USB hardware mappings that the caller has permission to see (Mapping.Modify, Mapping.Use, or Mapping.Audit on each entry). Pass check-node with a specific node name to validate that each mapping's physical USB device actually exists and is reachable on that node — errors are returned inline per mapping rather than as a top-level failure. Results are filtered by per-mapping permissions, so callers with restricted roles may see a partial list.

examples.summary: List all USB mappings and validate them against node pve1

tips: Omitting check-node returns mappings quickly with no node-side validation; include it before attaching a mapping to a VM to confirm the USB device is present.
The 'error' array on each mapping item is only populated when check-node is supplied; an empty or absent error array means the mapping passed validation on that node.
USB mappings are cluster-wide logical names — the 'map' array entries bind each node to its physical USB vendor:product or path.
